newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open firm,interest in electronics.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open firm,interest in electronics.

text.p: Singapore shares opened firm on Friday with some light buying interest in electronics stocks.
Dealers said the dealings were subdued with no fresh news to jolt the market out of its recent stupor.
"There seems to be some interest in electronic stocks but volume is light. It is probably because these stocks have bottomed out," said a trader with a local firm.
The SES electronics index touched a high of 77.22 before easing to 77.03, up 0.39 point after an hour of trading.
The Straits Times Industrials Index was up 5.94 points to 2,122.38. Volume was 23 million units with 80 up and 47 down.

Electronic Resources continued to see active dealings with several block trades done after news that three directors sold 10 million shares at S$1.40 ($0.99) on Thursday. It was up one cent to S$1.44 with 4.5 million shares traded including the block deals.
CAM International Holdings, also a electronics-based company, was also active with 1.3 million shares traded and was unchanged at S$0.795.
Early gainers include Singapore Press foreign, City Development and DBS foreign while losers were Singapore Land, DBS Land and Far East Levingston.
